facts.text: Long before settlers, Shelter Island was known as Manhansack‑aha‑quash‑awamock, a name meaning 'an island sheltered by islands' that echoed the Manhanset tribe’s peaceful home.
The Havens House, erected by the Havens family in the early 1700s, now serves as the Shelter Island History Museum and has survived war and harsh weather.
The Havens House became a museum in 1984 and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving its legacy for future generations.
The Perlman Music Program, founded in 1996 by violinist Isaac Perlman and his wife Toby, brings free classical concerts to Shelter Island’s residents.
In 2004, John Kerry became the first Democrat in recent history to win Shelter Island, signaling a notable political shift on the island.
